Part of [AGENTIC-2895](https://linear.app/agenticassets/issue/AGENTIC-2895).

This is a **synthetic-only, offline prototype**, not a live writer, production migration, or source acceptance path. The SQL draft uses a fixture-only schema and requires a specifically named database plus a session marker. Those tripwires and the disposable test server are not security isolation and do not authorize an apply. Production DDL requires ownership reconciliation, an independently reviewed migration, and the separate production approval gate. The prototype is not connected to the collector and does not consume real collector data.

The planner accepts only explicitly marked synthetic artifacts and fixture URLs at `example.test`. Its conservative screening rejects ordinary values including percent signs, URLs in attribute text, and many harmless credential-like words. Screening is not proof that secrets are absent. It cannot capture all source fields, identify canonical properties, establish coverage or availability, or reproduce the full source collection and ingestion workflow. Native IDs are recorded as unresolved evidence; ordinal and digest identify a capture within one immutable artifact and are not stable property identity. Changed observations in different synthetic generations remain separate; a divergent replay under the same generation and ordinal is rejected. Omitted attributes and missing or unsupported fixture identity or URL produce partial reporting. No result grants freshness, lifecycle, scheduling, or deletion authority.

The output SQL is created exclusively with restrictive file permissions and never follows an existing destination symlink. Parent directories and synthetic inputs are caller-controlled and are not sandboxed or independently authenticated. Keep outputs in an ignored private scratch directory; they contain input evidence. No database URL or production connection option exists.

From a standalone `git clone --no-hardlinks`, run `python3 -m pytest tests/test_cre_buildout_observation_prototype.py -q` and `python3 tests/run_buildout_observation_prototype_postgres.py --execute-disposable-fixture`. The latter creates a disposable local PostgreSQL server without a TCP listener, then removes it after the test. These fixture checks do not replace an independently reviewed security design, production data/ownership review, or larger end-to-end proof.

Fixture artifact reads reject final symlinks and use bounded single-descriptor pre/post change checks. Parent directories remain caller-controlled; these checks do not authenticate bytes or create an atomic multi-file snapshot. Native Windows lacks the required no-follow behavior and fails closed; use WSL.
